payload.text:
Don't merge yet. There's one serious permissions bug: **anyone with a view-only link can edit documents.** All the tests pass, but none of them cover this case. I only read and ran the code; nothing was changed.

**Blocker: `canEdit` in `src/guard.js` checks the wrong right**
```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```
JavaScript evaluates `===` before `&`, so this runs as `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, which is `mask & true`, which is `mask & 1`. That's the READ bit. So `canEdit` asks "can this person read?" instead of "can this person write?" I checked it directly:
- **Viewer** (READ only): `canEdit` → `true`. They can edit.
- **Comment and write rights but no READ**: `canEdit` → `0`, so they can't edit.

The tests miss it because the only editor they check also has READ. The fix is to use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE)`, the same way `canComment` does. It would also help to add a test that says "a viewer cannot edit".

**Smaller things in `transferOwnership` (`src/ownership.js`), worth a look:**
- **It doesn't check who's giving ownership away.** It never confirms that `fromUser` is actually `doc.owner`, so any caller can take ownership. That may be handled higher up, but nothing here enforces it.
- **The old owner can be left with no rights.** If `fromUser` has no share entry, `undefined & ~ADMIN` becomes `0`, which quietly creates a share with nothing in it.
- **Giving ownership to yourself loses nothing, but it's untested.** If `fromUser === toUser`, the new full-rights value overwrites the removal of ADMIN, so the result is fine.

**Looks fine:**
- `toggleRight` uses XOR, which matches the README ("on if off, off if on").
- `canComment` and the locking logic are correct.
- The changelog, README and version bump to 3.2.0 are consistent.
